subject: Renewal bridge and staged ramp with temporary grace period
messages:
From: Jane Dempsey <jdempsey@atlashealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: procurement@atlashealth.com
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion & staggered ramp ask

Hi Olga,

We're approaching our renewal window and want to discuss a slightly unusual request. We're planning a multi-year commitment but expect a big front-loaded usage for the first 90 days due to a product launch. We'd like to: 

- Keep total committed value across 36 months, but allow a temporary grace on overage for the initial 3 months (so initial burst doesn't immediately trigger penalties).
- Split invoicing so Q1 usage is billed on a staggered cadence (helps our cashflow).
- Co-term the renewal with one of our other vendor agreements (Nov boundary).

I've attached our procurement template and a high-level MAP (Atlas-MAP_v2.xlsx). Can you outline if Redwood can accept a bridge period for the initial ramp, and whether we can do staged invoicing plus co-terming?

Thanks,
Jane

Karthik / Marissa — forwarding Atlas Health's note. TL;DR: they want a 36-month commit, large front-loaded consumption for first 90 days, a 90-day grace on overage, and co-term with a Nov boundary. They also want staged invoicing.

As this touches pricing, billing, and contract language (grace period + invoicing cadence + co-term), can you confirm what levers we can apply and any constraints from finance/legal? Suggested immediate asks:
- Pricing concession (temporary overage forgiveness for first 90 days) — is a credit band viable?
- Staged invoicing approach (split Q1 into two invoices) — finance sign-off required.
- Contract language for temporary grace + automatic reversion to standard overage terms after 90 days.

I'll coordinate the amendment draft once we agree on the commercial terms.

On Thu, Oct 29, 2026 at 03:44 PM Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.inference.com> wrote:
> Karthik / Marissa — forwarding Atlas Health's note.

Thanks for the context, Olga. Quick thoughts:

1) Pricing credits: We can offer a temporary "ramp credit" that covers up to 60% of expected overage for the first 90 days, applied as a one-time invoice credit. This avoids permanently lowering unit pricing but helps their launch.
2) Staged invoicing: Finance will accept split-invoicing for the first billing period if they receive a documented schedule and commit to the overall net payment plan. Needs an approval from billing ops.
3) Co-terming: Legal usually ok with an amendment that aligns boundaries, but there may be a modest administrative fee to reschedule renewal dates — we should present as an implementation charge rather than a discount.

Marissa — will you draft the amended language for the 90-day grace and the ramp-credit? I'll loop billing to confirm staged invoicing cadence. If acceptable, we can present a single amendment (no multiple docs).

Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Head of Sales Operations

Hi Jane — thanks for the clear ask and the MAP. Great to hear about your product launch — congrats.

We can absolutely accommodate a short-term ramp accommodation. Proposed commercial structure:

- Term: 36 months, co-terming to 2029-11-30 boundary.
- Ramp credit: Redwood will apply a one-time invoice credit equal to 50% of overage above the committed baseline for the first 90 days post-go-live (applies only to token overages tied to public launch traffic).
- Staged invoicing: Q1 post-go-live will be invoiced in two equal invoices (day 30 and day 75); subsequent billing returns to normal cadence.
- Admin fee: a one-time implementation fee of $5,000 to align contract boundaries and process the co-term will be applied on the first invoice.

I've attached a draft amendment with the suggested language for the 90-day grace and credit mechanics (rdw-amendment-staircase-draft.pdf). Please review and confirm the go-live window so we can lock the dates.

Next steps:
- Jane: confirm go-live target and whether the MAP consumption estimates are accurate.
- Atlas procurement: confirm staged invoicing is acceptable.
- Olga/Karthik: I need final approval on the $5k admin fee and the ramp-credit band (50% is proposed).

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Renewal Manager, Redwood Inference
